title: Those Singhs as were camping on the hill side,

blocks.text: Those Singhs as were camping on the hill side tried again to climb out of the trap, but hill troops guarded the ridges and blocked every pass. From above came stones, bricks and bullets, while Rajput positions added cannon fire that tore through anyone who tried to force a way upward.

Even under that barrage, the Singhs briefly seized one enemy post before superior numbers pushed them back. Refusing to give up the ascent, they dug trenches and underground bunkers wherever they could, using knives, daggers, spears, and swords to carve footholds into the slope.

That improvised fieldwork let them renew the climb with more order and protection. By sheer persistence they won another hold on the hillside and began cutting some earth with swords for making steps so that men and horses could continue moving above the river.
